questions.q: Is a rock alive?
questions.hint: Does a rock eat, grow, or breathe?
questions.fix: A rock is not alive. Living things grow, need food and water, and make more of their kind.

questions.q: Is a tree alive?
questions.hint: Does a tree grow bigger every year?
questions.fix: A tree is alive. It grows, drinks water through its roots, and makes seeds.

questions.q: What do all living things need to stay alive?
questions.hint: You drink it when you are thirsty.
questions.fix: Every living thing needs water. Toys and shoes are nice, but plants and animals need water.

questions.q: A baby frog that swims and has a tail is called a...
questions.hint: It starts with T, like tail.
questions.fix: A baby frog is a tadpole. It swims with a tail, then grows legs and becomes a frog.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.fix: A caterpillar grows, makes a chrysalis, and comes out as a butterfly.

questions.q: What hatches out of a chicken egg?
questions.fix: A baby chicken, called a chick, hatches out of the egg.

questions.q: Which animal has feathers?
questions.hint: It might sing in a tree.
questions.fix: Birds are the only animals with feathers.

questions.q: Where does a fish live?
questions.fix: Fish live in water and breathe with gills.

questions.q: Which one is a baby dog?
questions.hint: It can wag a tiny tail.
questions.fix: A baby dog is a puppy. A lamb is a baby sheep, and a cub can be a baby bear or lion.

questions.q: What do you call an animal that eats only plants?
questions.hint: Think of a cow munching grass.
questions.fix: An animal that eats only plants is a plant eater, also called an herbivore. Cows and rabbits are plant eaters.

questions.q: Which animal is a mammal with fur?
questions.fix: A bear has fur and feeds its babies milk, so it is a mammal. Snakes have scales and frogs have smooth skin.

questions.q: Which one grows into a big oak tree?
questions.fix: An acorn is the seed of an oak tree. Plant it and a tiny oak can grow.

questions.q: Which home is a bird's?
questions.hint: Birds build it out of twigs.
questions.fix: Many birds build nests for their eggs. Spiders make webs, and bees live in hives.

questions.q: Which animal lays eggs?
questions.fix: Ducks lay eggs. Cows and horses have babies that are born alive.

questions.q: What do baby mammals drink from their mother?
questions.hint: It is white and comes from mom.
questions.fix: Baby mammals drink milk from their mothers. That is one thing all mammals have in common.

questions.q: Is a toy robot alive?
questions.hint: Does it grow up and have babies?
questions.fix: A toy robot is not alive. It cannot grow, eat, or make babies, even if it moves.

questions.q: Which animal changes from a tadpole to a grown-up?
questions.fix: Frogs start as tadpoles in the water and grow into frogs.

questions.q: Which of these lived long, long ago and is now gone?
questions.fix: Dinosaurs lived a very long time ago. People learn about them from fossils.

questions.q: A living thing that makes its own food from sunlight is called a...
questions.fix: A producer makes its own food. Green plants are producers because they use sunlight to make food.

questions.q: Mushrooms and worms that break down dead leaves are called...
questions.hint: They de-compose, or break things down.
questions.fix: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.q: An animal that hunts other animals for food is called a...
questions.hint: A hawk chasing a mouse is one.
questions.fix: A predator hunts other animals. The animal being hunted is called prey.

questions.q: In a food chain, grass is eaten by a rabbit. What might eat the rabbit?
questions.hint: Think of an animal that eats meat.
questions.fix: A fox could eat the rabbit. Food chains go from plants to plant eaters to meat eaters.

questions.q: What do you call the tiny building blocks that make up every living thing?
questions.hint: You need a microscope to see most of them.
questions.fix: Cells are the tiny building blocks of living things. Your body is made of trillions of them.

questions.q: What are the four stages in a butterfly's life cycle?
questions.hint: It starts as an egg on a leaf.
questions.fix: A butterfly goes from egg to caterpillar to chrysalis to butterfly. That big change is called metamorphosis.

questions.q: What is the big word for when an animal changes body shape as it grows, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly?
questions.fix: Metamorphosis means a big change in body form, like caterpillar to butterfly or tadpole to frog.

questions.q: Animals with a backbone are called...
questions.hint: Vertebra is a bone in your back.
questions.fix: Animals with backbones are vertebrates. Fish, frogs, snakes, birds and mammals all have backbones.

questions.q: Which animal is an invertebrate, with no backbone?
questions.fix: A jellyfish has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate. Sharks and parrots have backbones.

questions.q: Which group of animals has smooth, damp skin and usually starts life in water?
questions.fix: Amphibians, like frogs and salamanders, have damp skin and usually start life in water.

questions.q: Snakes, lizards and turtles have dry, scaly skin. What group are they in?
questions.hint: Crocodiles are in this group too.
questions.fix: They are reptiles. Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

questions.q: A dolphin breathes air and feeds its babies milk. What kind of animal is it?
questions.hint: Dogs and people are in this group too.
questions.fix: A dolphin is a mammal, not a fish. It comes up to breathe air through its blowhole.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal's color helps it blend in with its surroundings?
questions.hint: Soldiers wear clothes with this pattern.
questions.fix: That is camouflage. It helps animals hide from predators or sneak up on prey.

questions.q: When a kind of animal is gone forever and none are left alive, it is...
questions.fix: An extinct animal has no living members left. Endangered means there are only a few left.

questions.q: Scientists say birds are living relatives of which animals?
questions.hint: Think of a T. rex and a chicken.
questions.fix: Birds come from a group of dinosaurs. That is why scientists call birds living dinosaurs.

questions.q: What is the place where an animal naturally lives and finds food, water and shelter?
questions.hint: A pond is one for a frog.
questions.fix: A habitat is an animal's natural home. A pond, a forest and a desert are all habitats.

questions.q: What tool helps scientists see things too tiny for their eyes, like cells?
questions.fix: A microscope makes tiny things look bigger. A telescope is for faraway things like stars.

questions.q: A frog egg hatches into a tadpole. What does the tadpole breathe with at first?
questions.fix: Young tadpoles breathe with gills, like fish. As they grow into frogs, most grow lungs.

questions.q: Which scientist studies living things?
questions.fix: A biologist studies living things. Geologists study rocks, and astronomers study space.

questions.q: An animal that eats both plants and meat is called...
questions.fix: An omnivore eats both plants and animals. Bears and people are omnivores.

questions.q: What big, bright star do you see in the daytime sky?
questions.fix: The Sun is a star, and it is the one closest to Earth. Never look straight at it.

questions.q: What do you often see in the sky at night that changes shape over the month?
questions.hint: Sometimes it looks like a banana, sometimes a ball.
questions.fix: The Moon looks like it changes shape. Those shapes are called phases.

questions.q: What is the name of the planet people live on?
questions.hint: It is mostly blue with oceans.
questions.fix: People live on planet Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.fix: Mars looks red because its dusty ground has rusty iron in it.

questions.q: Which planet has big, bright rings you can see in pictures?
questions.fix: Saturn has the brightest, best-known rings, made of ice and rock.

questions.q: Who goes into space in a rocket?
questions.fix: Astronauts travel to space. They train for a long time first.

questions.q: What hot, melted rock comes out of a volcano?
questions.fix: Lava is melted rock that flows out of a volcano.

questions.q: Is the ocean water salty or sweet?
questions.fix: Ocean water is salty. Most rivers and lakes have fresh water.

questions.q: What do you call a very big, tall hill with a pointy top?
questions.fix: A mountain is land that rises very high.

questions.q: When it is daytime, which way does the sun rise?
questions.hint: The opposite side from where it sets.
questions.fix: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

questions.q: Which is bigger, the Sun or the Earth?
questions.hint: It only looks small because it is far away.
questions.fix: The Sun is much, much bigger than Earth. It looks small because it is so far away.

questions.q: What is a shape made by stars in the night sky called?
questions.hint: The Big Dipper is part of one.
questions.fix: A constellation is a group of stars that people imagine as a picture.

questions.q: What do you call a rock or bone print from an animal that lived long ago?
questions.hint: Dinosaur bones in a museum are these.
questions.fix: A fossil is what is left of a living thing from long ago, saved in rock.

questions.q: Where do you find sand, shells and waves?
questions.hint: You might build a sandcastle there.
questions.fix: A beach is where land meets water. Waves bring sand and shells.

questions.q: What is a hole in the ground where some animals like bats live called?
questions.fix: A cave is a big hollow space underground or in a hillside.

questions.q: Which is the hottest: the Sun, an ice cube or a snowball?
questions.hint: It is a giant ball of hot gas.
questions.fix: The Sun is hottest. It is a huge ball of very hot glowing gas.

questions.q: Does the Moon make its own light?
questions.fix: The Moon does not make light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it.

questions.q: What is the ground shaking hard called?
questions.fix: An earthquake is when the ground shakes because rock deep underground moves.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.hint: It is also the smallest planet.
questions.fix: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and the smallest.

questions.q: Which planet that goes around the Sun is the biggest?
questions.hint: Look for a huge red storm spot on it.
questions.fix: Jupiter is the biggest planet. Its Great Red Spot is a huge storm.

questions.q: How many planets are in the solar system?
questions.hint: Pluto is now called a dwarf planet.
questions.fix: There are eight planets. Pluto is called a dwarf planet.

questions.q: How long does it take Earth to travel once around the Sun?
questions.fix: Earth takes about one year to go around the Sun once.

questions.q: Earth spins all the way around once in about how long?
questions.hint: From one sunrise to the next.
questions.fix: Earth spins once about every 24 hours. That spin gives day and night.

questions.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.hint: The planet turns like a top.
questions.fix: Earth spins. The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night.

questions.q: What is the hot, melted rock called while it is still underground?
questions.hint: Above ground it gets a different name.
questions.fix: Underground it is magma. When it flows out of a volcano, it is called lava.

questions.q: What kind of rock forms when lava or magma cools and hardens?
questions.fix: Igneous rock forms from cooled melted rock. Granite and basalt are igneous.

questions.q: Rock made from layers of sand, mud and shells pressed together over time is...
questions.hint: Sediment is bits of sand and mud.
questions.fix: Sedimentary rock forms in layers. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary, and fossils are often found in it.

questions.q: What is it called when wind and water slowly wear away rock and soil?
questions.fix: That is erosion. Over a very long time, a river can carve a deep canyon.

questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.hint: It lies between Asia and the Americas.
questions.fix: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

questions.q: What do you call a huge mass of ice that creeps slowly downhill?
questions.hint: It starts with G and moves very slowly.
questions.fix: A glacier is a huge mass of ice that slowly moves downhill.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy the solar system is in?
questions.hint: It sounds like a candy bar.
questions.fix: The solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: When the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun, it is a...
questions.fix: That is a solar eclipse. In a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

questions.q: What tool helps people see faraway stars and planets?
questions.fix: A telescope makes faraway things look closer.

questions.q: Which star is close to straight above the North Pole and helps travelers find north?
questions.fix: The North Star, Polaris, sits almost right above the North Pole, so it helps people find north.

questions.q: What do you call a hot spring that shoots water and steam high into the air?
questions.hint: Old Faithful in Yellowstone is one.
questions.fix: A geyser is a spring that sprays hot water and steam. Old Faithful is a famous one.

questions.q: What is the very center of Earth called?
questions.hint: Like the center of an apple.
questions.fix: The center is the core. The outside layer is the crust, and the mantle is in between.

questions.q: What is the thin, rocky outer layer of Earth that people walk on?
questions.fix: The crust is Earth's outer layer. It is thin compared with the rest of the planet.

questions.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape during a month?
questions.a: Different amounts of its sunlit side face Earth
wrong: It gets bitten by space rocks
questions.hint: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun.
questions.fix: As the Moon goes around Earth, people see different amounts of its sunny side. Those are the phases.

questions.q: What happens to an ice cube on a warm, sunny day?
questions.fix: Warmth melts ice. The solid ice turns into liquid water.

questions.q: What sticks to a magnet?
questions.fix: Magnets pull on things with iron in them, like a steel paper clip. Wood and plastic do not stick.

questions.q: If you drop a ball, which way does it go?
questions.fix: Gravity pulls things down toward the ground.

questions.q: Will a rock sink or float in water?
questions.fix: A rock sinks because it is heavy for its size.

questions.q: What do you get when water freezes?
questions.fix: When water gets cold enough it freezes into ice.

questions.q: Is a push or a pull what you use to open a drawer toward you?
questions.hint: You bring it closer to you.
questions.fix: Bringing something toward you is a pull. Pushes move things away.

questions.q: What do you see when light is blocked by your body on a sunny day?
questions.fix: Your body blocks the light and makes a shadow.

questions.q: Which is a liquid?
questions.fix: Milk is a liquid. Liquids can be poured and take the shape of their cup.

questions.q: Which one makes a sound when you hit it?
questions.fix: A drum makes a loud sound when you hit it because it shakes, or vibrates.

questions.q: Which is easier to roll across the floor?
questions.fix: A round ball rolls easily. A box slides or tips instead.

questions.q: What makes a flashlight shine?
questions.fix: A battery gives electricity to the bulb so it lights up.

questions.q: Which is the hottest?
questions.a: A stove burner that is on
questions.fix: A stove that is on is very hot. Ice pops and snowmen are cold.

questions.q: What does a mirror do with light?
questions.hint: You can see yourself in it.
questions.fix: A mirror reflects, or bounces back, light. That is how you see yourself.

questions.q: What comes out of a pot of very hot, boiling water?
questions.hint: It looks like a little cloud.
questions.fix: Boiling water turns into steam, a gas. Stay back, steam is hot!

questions.q: Which is heavier: a bowling ball or a feather?
questions.hint: Which one would be hard to lift?
questions.fix: A bowling ball is much heavier than a feather.

questions.q: What do you call something solid, like a block, that keeps its own shape?
questions.fix: A solid keeps its shape. Liquids spill and gases spread out.

questions.q: What sound does a tight rubber band make when you pluck it?
questions.fix: A plucked rubber band vibrates and makes a twang sound.

questions.q: What helps a sled slide down a snowy hill?
questions.hint: It is the same pull that makes things fall.
questions.fix: Gravity pulls the sled down the hill.

questions.q: What are the three common states of matter?
questions.fix: Matter is usually a solid, a liquid or a gas, like ice, water and steam.

questions.q: What is it called when liquid water turns into a gas?
questions.hint: A puddle disappears on a sunny day.
questions.fix: That is evaporation. Heat turns liquid water into water vapor.

questions.q: Water drops form on the outside of a cold glass of lemonade. What is this called?
questions.hint: Water vapor in the air turns back into liquid.
questions.fix: That is condensation. Water vapor from the air cools on the glass and becomes liquid drops.

questions.q: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees on which temperature scale?
questions.hint: The scale is named after Anders Celsius.
questions.fix: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level. That is 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.hint: It is why apples fall from trees.
questions.fix: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth. It also keeps the Moon going around Earth.

questions.q: What force slows a ball rolling across grass?
questions.fix: Friction happens when surfaces rub, and it slows things down. It is stronger on rough grass than on a smooth floor.

questions.q: The ends of a bar magnet are called its...
questions.hint: Like the North and South ones on Earth.
questions.fix: A magnet has a north pole and a south pole.

questions.q: If you put the north poles of two magnets together, what happens?
questions.hint: Like poles do not like each other.
questions.fix: Like poles repel, or push apart. A north pole and a south pole attract.

questions.q: What is a ramp called as a simple machine?
questions.fix: A ramp is an inclined plane. It lets you move a load up with less force.

questions.q: A seesaw is which kind of simple machine?
questions.hint: It has a balance point in the middle.
questions.fix: A seesaw is a lever. The balance point is called the fulcrum.

questions.q: A rope over a wheel used to lift a flag up a pole is a...
questions.hint: Pull the rope down, the flag goes up.
questions.fix: That is a pulley. It can change the direction of a pull.

questions.q: Sound is made when something does what very quickly?
questions.hint: Touch your throat while you hum.
questions.fix: Sound comes from vibrations, quick back-and-forth shakes.

questions.q: Which travels faster: light or sound?
questions.hint: Think about seeing lightning before hearing thunder.
questions.fix: Light is much faster than sound. That is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

questions.q: What is the path that electricity flows around, like battery to bulb and back, called?
questions.fix: A circuit is a complete loop. If the loop is broken, the bulb goes out.

questions.q: Which material is a good conductor that lets electricity flow through it?
questions.hint: Wires are often made of it.
questions.fix: Copper is a metal that conducts electricity well. Rubber and wood are insulators.

questions.q: What is a material that blocks heat or electricity, like the rubber on a wire, called?
questions.hint: It keeps things in, like a warm blanket.
questions.fix: An insulator blocks the flow of heat or electricity.

questions.q: A glass prism splits white light into what?
questions.fix: A prism bends light and spreads white light into all the colors of the rainbow.

questions.q: When sugar disappears as you stir it into water, it...
questions.hint: It mixes in so well you cannot see it.
questions.fix: Sugar dissolves in water. The water still tastes sweet because the sugar is still there.

questions.q: What kind of energy does a moving car, a rolling ball or a running dog have?
questions.hint: Its science name is kinetic energy.
questions.fix: Anything moving has motion energy, also called kinetic energy.

questions.q: A balloon rubbed on your hair can stick to the wall. What is this?
questions.hint: It can also make your hair stand up.
questions.fix: Rubbing builds up static electricity, which makes the balloon cling.

questions.q: What do you use to see?
questions.fix: You see with your eyes.

questions.q: What do you use to hear?
questions.hint: They are on the sides of your head.
questions.fix: You hear with your ears.

questions.q: What do you use to smell a flower?
questions.fix: You smell with your nose.

questions.q: What part of your body pumps blood?
questions.hint: Feel it go thump thump in your chest.
questions.fix: Your heart pumps blood all around your body.

questions.q: What do you use to breathe in air?
questions.hint: They fill up like balloons in your chest.
questions.fix: Your lungs take in air when you breathe.

questions.q: What hard parts are inside your body and hold you up?
questions.hint: A skeleton is made of them.
questions.fix: Bones hold you up and make your skeleton.

questions.q: What should you do before you eat to wash away germs?
questions.fix: Washing your hands with soap and water helps wash germs away.

questions.q: What do you use to taste food?
questions.fix: Your tongue tastes sweet, salty, sour and more.

questions.q: What part of you does the thinking?
questions.fix: Your brain does your thinking, remembering and dreaming.

questions.q: Where does the food you swallow go?
questions.fix: Swallowed food goes down to your stomach to be broken down.

questions.q: What covers the outside of your whole body?
questions.hint: You can feel touches with it.
questions.fix: Skin covers your body and lets you feel touch, warm and cold.

questions.q: What helps your body move, like when you lift your arm?
questions.fix: Muscles pull on your bones to move your body.

questions.q: What protects your brain like a helmet?
questions.hint: It is the bone in your head.
questions.fix: Your skull is a strong bone that protects your brain.

questions.q: What do you use to chew food?
questions.fix: You chew with your teeth. Brushing keeps them healthy.

questions.q: When you run fast, what happens to your heart?
questions.hint: Put your hand on your chest after jumping.
questions.fix: Your heart beats faster when you exercise to send more blood to your muscles.

questions.q: Why do you cover your mouth when you sneeze?
questions.fix: Covering a sneeze keeps germs from flying onto other people.

questions.q: What does your body need every night to grow and rest?
questions.fix: Sleep helps your body rest, grow and get ready for a new day.

questions.q: What is the colored circle in your eye called?
questions.fix: The colored part of your eye is the iris. It can be brown, blue, green and more.

questions.q: Which organ is the largest one in the human body?
questions.fix: Skin is the body's largest organ.

questions.q: Which is the hardest material in the human body?
questions.fix: Tooth enamel, the outer layer of teeth, is the hardest material in the body.

questions.q: Which bone, up in your thigh, is the longest one you have?
questions.hint: It is in your upper leg.
questions.fix: The femur, your thigh bone, is longer than any other bone you have.

questions.q: What tubes carry blood around the body?
questions.hint: Veins and arteries are two kinds.
questions.fix: Blood vessels carry blood. Arteries carry it away from the heart and veins bring it back.

questions.q: Which bones make a cage that protects your heart and lungs?
questions.fix: Your ribs form the rib cage, which protects your heart and lungs.

questions.q: What dark circle in the middle of your eye lets light in?
questions.hint: It gets smaller in bright light.
questions.fix: The pupil lets light into the eye. It shrinks in bright light and widens in the dark.

questions.q: Which gas does your body need from the air you breathe in?
questions.fix: Your body needs oxygen. You breathe out carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which gas do you breathe out?
questions.hint: Plants use it to make food.
questions.fix: You breathe out carbon dioxide. Plants take it in to make their food.

questions.q: What liquid in your mouth starts breaking down food as you chew?
questions.fix: Saliva, or spit, starts breaking down food even before you swallow.

questions.q: Which blood cells help fight germs?
questions.hint: They are named for a color, but not red.
questions.fix: White blood cells fight germs. Red blood cells carry oxygen.

questions.q: What do red blood cells carry around the body?
questions.fix: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.

questions.q: The heart is a special kind of what?
questions.hint: It squeezes all day and night.
questions.fix: The heart is a muscle that squeezes to pump blood.

questions.q: Which body system includes the brain, spinal cord and nerves?
questions.fix: The nervous system carries messages between your brain and your body.

questions.q: Which body system breaks down food?
questions.hint: Mouth, stomach and intestines are part of it.
questions.fix: The digestive system breaks food down so your body can use it.

questions.q: What muscle under your lungs helps you breathe in?
questions.hint: It starts with D and has a silent G.
questions.fix: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle under your lungs that helps you breathe.

questions.q: What connects muscles to bones?
questions.hint: There is a big one at the back of your ankle.
questions.fix: Tendons connect muscles to bones, like the Achilles tendon at your heel.

questions.q: What do you call the places where two bones meet, like your knee and elbow?
questions.fix: Joints are where bones meet. They let you bend and turn.

questions.q: Which sense uses the tiny bumps on your tongue called taste buds?
questions.fix: Taste buds on your tongue let you taste.

questions.q: Where in your body is the teeny bone called the stirrup?
questions.fix: The stirrup, or stapes, is a tiny bone inside the ear.

questions.q: What is the long tube that food passes through after the stomach, where most nutrients are taken in?
questions.hint: It is small in width but very long.
questions.fix: The small intestine takes in most nutrients from food. It is long and folded up in your belly.

questions.q: What falls from clouds on a rainy day?
questions.fix: Rain is water drops falling from clouds.

questions.q: What cold, white flakes fall in winter in some places?
questions.fix: Snowflakes are made of ice and fall when it is very cold.

questions.q: What do you see in the sky after rain when the sun comes out?
questions.fix: A rainbow shows up when sunlight shines through raindrops.

questions.q: What makes a kite fly?
questions.hint: You cannot see it, but you can feel it.
questions.fix: Wind is moving air, and it lifts the kite.

questions.q: What loud boom comes after lightning?
questions.fix: Thunder is the sound lightning makes.

questions.q: What should you wear on a cold, snowy day?
questions.fix: A warm coat keeps your body heat in on a cold day.

questions.q: What tool tells you how hot or cold it is?
questions.fix: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.q: Which season is usually the hottest?
questions.fix: Summer is usually the warmest season.

questions.q: In which season do many trees lose their leaves?
questions.fix: In fall, or autumn, many trees drop their colorful leaves.

questions.q: What are clouds made of?
questions.a: Tiny drops of water or ice
questions.hint: They look fluffy but they are wet.
questions.fix: Clouds are made of tiny water drops or tiny bits of ice floating in the air.

questions.q: Where is a safe place to be in a thunderstorm?
questions.fix: Go inside during a thunderstorm. Trees and water are not safe from lightning.

questions.q: What season comes after winter?
questions.fix: After winter comes spring, when many plants start to grow again.

questions.q: What kind of weather is it when the sun shines and there are no clouds?
questions.fix: No clouds and lots of sun means sunny weather.

questions.q: What is a cloud that sits right on the ground called?
questions.hint: It makes it hard to see far away.
questions.fix: Fog is a cloud close to the ground.

questions.q: Balls of ice that fall in some storms are called...
questions.hint: They can bounce on the ground.
questions.fix: Hail is lumps of ice that fall from some thunderstorms.

questions.q: What weather do you need to make puddles to jump in?
questions.fix: Rain makes puddles.

questions.q: Which one helps you stay dry in the rain?
questions.hint: You hold it over your head.
questions.fix: An umbrella keeps raindrops off you.

questions.q: What is a strong, spinning wind shaped like a funnel?
questions.hint: It twists down from a storm cloud.
questions.fix: A tornado is a spinning column of air that reaches down from a storm.

questions.q: What tool measures how fast the wind is blowing?
questions.hint: It has little cups that spin.
questions.fix: An anemometer measures wind speed. Its cups spin faster in stronger wind.

questions.q: A weather vane tells you what about the wind?
questions.fix: A weather vane shows which direction the wind is coming from.

questions.q: What tool collects rain so you can measure how much fell?
questions.fix: A rain gauge catches rain so you can see how much fell.

questions.q: What do you call water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail?
questions.fix: Any water falling from clouds is precipitation.

questions.q: In the water cycle, what happens right after water vapor cools high in the sky?
questions.hint: Remember drops on a cold glass.
questions.fix: Cooling vapor condenses into tiny drops that make clouds.

questions.q: What powers the water cycle by heating water so it evaporates?
questions.fix: The Sun's heat makes water evaporate and keeps the water cycle going.

questions.q: A huge spinning storm that forms over warm ocean water is a...
questions.hint: It has a calm eye in the middle.
questions.fix: A hurricane forms over warm ocean water and has a calm center called the eye.

questions.q: A long time with much less rain than usual is called a...
questions.hint: Plants dry up and the ground cracks.
questions.fix: A drought is a long dry spell with little rain.

questions.q: A big snowstorm with strong winds and blowing snow is a...
questions.hint: It makes it hard to see.
questions.fix: A blizzard is a snowstorm with strong winds.

questions.q: What kind of scientist studies and forecasts the weather?
questions.hint: It has nothing to do with meteors!
questions.fix: A meteorologist studies the weather and makes forecasts.

questions.q: High, thin, wispy clouds made of ice crystals are called...
questions.hint: They look like feathers or curls of hair.
questions.fix: Cirrus clouds are high, wispy and made of ice crystals.

questions.q: Puffy, white clouds that look like cotton balls are called...
questions.hint: They are the ones you find shapes in.
questions.fix: Cumulus clouds are puffy and white, often on nice days.

questions.q: Tall, dark clouds that bring thunderstorms are called...
questions.fix: Cumulonimbus clouds are tall storm clouds that bring thunder, lightning and heavy rain.

questions.q: What is the mix of gases around Earth that people breathe called?
questions.hint: It is like a blanket of air around the planet.
questions.fix: The atmosphere is the layer of air around Earth.

questions.q: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
questions.fix: Light reaches you almost at once, but sound takes longer to travel.

questions.q: What causes the seasons on Earth?
questions.a: Earth's tilt as it goes around the Sun
wrong: Earth getting much closer and farther from the Sun
questions.hint: Earth leans a little to one side.
questions.fix: Earth is tilted. As it goes around the Sun, each half gets more direct sunlight for part of the year.

questions.q: Raindrops that freeze into little ice pellets before they reach the ground are called...
questions.fix: Sleet is small ice pellets that freeze on the way down.

questions.q: Water drops that form on grass on a cool morning are called...
questions.fix: Dew forms when water vapor in the air condenses on cool grass.

questions.q: What is the name for the weather a place usually has over many years?
questions.hint: A desert has a dry one.
questions.fix: Climate is the usual weather of a place over a long time. Weather is what happens today.

questions.q: What instrument measures air pressure to help forecast the weather?
questions.fix: A barometer measures air pressure. Falling pressure can mean a storm is coming.

questions.q: What part of a plant grows under the ground and drinks water?
questions.hint: They hold the plant in the soil.
questions.fix: Roots grow underground, hold the plant in place and soak up water.

questions.q: What do plants need from the sky to grow?
questions.fix: Plants need sunlight to make their food.

questions.q: What color are most leaves in summer?
questions.fix: Most leaves are green in summer.

questions.q: What do bees visit to collect nectar?
questions.hint: They are colorful and smell nice.
questions.fix: Bees visit flowers for nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower.

questions.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
questions.fix: A seed needs water and warmth to sprout.

questions.q: Which animal has a very long neck?
questions.hint: It eats leaves from tall trees.
questions.fix: The giraffe has a very long neck and is the tallest land animal.

questions.q: Which animal has a trunk?
questions.fix: An elephant uses its trunk to smell, drink and grab food.

questions.q: Which animal hops and carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.fix: Kangaroo moms carry their babies, called joeys, in a pouch.

questions.q: Which animal has black and white stripes?
questions.hint: It looks like a striped horse.
questions.fix: A zebra has black and white stripes.

questions.q: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.hint: Count the legs on an ant.
questions.fix: Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight, so spiders are not insects.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.hint: Same as an octopus has arms.
questions.fix: Spiders have eight legs.

questions.q: Which animal is awake at night and says hoo-hoo?
questions.fix: Most owls are awake at night. Animals that are busy at night are called nocturnal.

questions.q: What does a cactus have to protect itself?
questions.fix: A cactus has sharp spines. It also stores water in its thick stem.

questions.q: What does a baby cat get called?
questions.fix: A baby cat is a kitten.

questions.q: Which animal has a shell it can hide in?
questions.fix: A turtle can pull its head into its hard shell.

questions.q: Which fruit grows on a tree: an apple or a carrot?
questions.hint: A carrot grows in the ground.
questions.fix: Apples grow on trees. Carrots are roots that grow underground.

questions.q: Which bird cannot fly but is a great swimmer?
questions.fix: Penguins cannot fly, but they swim very well with their flippers.

questions.q: What do caterpillars mostly eat?
questions.fix: Most caterpillars munch on leaves.

questions.q: What is the process plants use to make food from sunlight, water and air?
questions.fix: Photosynthesis is how plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

questions.q: What green material in leaves captures sunlight?
questions.fix: Chlorophyll is the green material that captures sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.q: What gas do plants give off that animals need to breathe?
questions.fix: Plants give off oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.q: What yellow dust do bees carry from flower to flower?
questions.fix: Bees carry pollen between flowers. That helps flowers make seeds.

questions.q: Moving pollen from one flower to another is called...
questions.fix: That is pollination. Bees, butterflies, birds and wind can all pollinate flowers.

questions.q: What is the long, deep winter sleep some animals take called?
questions.hint: Some bears and ground squirrels do it.
questions.fix: Hibernation is a long, deep rest through the winter that saves energy.

questions.q: When birds fly south for the winter and come back in spring, it is called...
questions.hint: Many geese do this every year.
questions.fix: Migration is a long trip animals make each year, often to find food or warmer weather.

questions.q: Trees that lose all their leaves in the fall are called...
questions.hint: It is the opposite of evergreen.
questions.fix: Deciduous trees drop their leaves in fall. Evergreens like pine trees keep their needles.

questions.q: Bats find their way in the dark by making sounds and listening for echoes. What is this called?
questions.fix: Echolocation means using echoes to find things. Bats and dolphins use it.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.hint: It is a spotted big cat.
questions.fix: The cheetah is the fastest land animal over short sprints.

questions.q: What is the largest animal ever known to live on Earth?
questions.fix: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

questions.q: What is the largest fish in the world?
questions.hint: Careful, a whale is not a fish.
questions.fix: The whale shark is the largest fish. A blue whale is bigger, but it is a mammal.

questions.q: A camel's hump stores mostly what?
questions.hint: It is energy for long trips.
questions.fix: A camel's hump stores fat, not water. The fat is energy for long desert trips.

questions.q: What are a kangaroo's babies called?
questions.fix: Baby kangaroos are joeys. Baby koalas are also called joeys.

questions.q: Animals like kangaroos and koalas whose babies grow in a pouch are called...
questions.fix: Kangaroos and koalas are marsupials, mammals whose babies grow in a pouch.

questions.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.fix: An octopus has eight arms.

questions.q: A sea star is not a fish. What does it use to move along the sea floor?
questions.fix: Sea stars move on hundreds of tiny tube feet under their arms.

questions.q: What do you call the part of a plant that grows into a new plant?
questions.fix: A seed holds a baby plant and food to help it start growing.

questions.q: Which part of a plant carries water up from the roots to the leaves?
questions.hint: On a tree it is the trunk.
questions.fix: The stem carries water up and holds the plant up. A tree trunk is a woody stem.

questions.q: Animals that are busy at night and sleep during the day are called...
questions.fix: Nocturnal animals, like most owls and bats, are active at night.

questions.q: What will this bug flutter around looking for?
questions.fix: Butterflies visit flowers to sip nectar.

questions.q: This animal hops and says ribbit. What was it when it was a baby?
questions.hint: It swam in a pond with a tail.
questions.fix: A frog starts as a tadpole.

questions.q: Where does this prickly plant grow best?
questions.hint: It can go a long time without rain.
questions.fix: Cactus plants grow well in dry deserts. They store water in their stems.

questions.q: What is this mountain that can erupt?
questions.hint: Hot lava can pour out of the top.
questions.fix: That is a volcano. Melted rock can come out of it.

questions.q: What two things help make this?
questions.hint: It can appear after a rain shower.
questions.fix: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops.

questions.q: Can this bird fly?
questions.hint: It uses its flippers to swim.
questions.fix: Penguins cannot fly. They are excellent swimmers.

questions.q: What does this animal reach with its long neck?
questions.hint: It is the tallest land animal.
questions.fix: A giraffe stretches its long neck to eat leaves high in the trees.

questions.q: What is this shape of the Moon called?
questions.hint: It looks like a banana or a smile.
questions.fix: A thin curved Moon is called a crescent.

questions.q: When the whole Moon looks round and bright, what is it called?
questions.hint: It looks like a big round cookie.
questions.fix: A full round Moon is called a full moon.

questions.q: Will this magnet pull the paper clip toward it?
questions.hint: The paper clip is made of steel.
questions.fix: Yes! A magnet pulls on steel paper clips.

questions.q: The red line on this thermometer is very high. Is it hot or cold?
questions.fix: A high red line means it is hot.

questions.q: Look at the plant. What is the part under the ground called?
questions.fix: The part under the ground is the roots. They drink up water.

questions.q: What loud sound comes after this flash?
questions.fix: Thunder comes after lightning.

questions.q: Which sense does this body part help with?
questions.fix: Eyes help you see.

questions.q: Which sense does this body part help with?
questions.fix: Ears help you hear.

questions.q: What happens to ice when it gets warm?
questions.fix: Warm ice melts into liquid water.

questions.q: What is this big animal's long nose called?
questions.hint: It can spray water with it.
questions.fix: An elephant's long nose is called a trunk.

questions.q: How many arms does this animal have?
questions.fix: An octopus has eight arms.

questions.q: This animal lives in the ocean. Is it a fish or a mammal?
questions.hint: It breathes air through a blowhole.
questions.fix: A dolphin is a mammal. It breathes air and feeds its babies milk.

questions.q: Is this animal an insect?
questions.hint: Count its legs: there are eight.
questions.fix: Spiders have eight legs, so they are arachnids, not insects.

questions.q: Name this planet, famous for its bright rings.
questions.hint: Count out from the Sun: it is number six.
questions.fix: That is Saturn. Its rings are made of ice and rock.

questions.q: Look at the circuit. Will the bulb light up?
wrong: No, batteries do not make light
questions.hint: Follow the wire all the way around.
questions.fix: The wire makes a complete loop from the battery to the bulb and back, so it lights.

questions.q: Look at this circuit with a gap in the wire. Will the bulb light up?
questions.fix: There is a gap, so electricity cannot flow and the bulb stays dark.

questions.q: The sun is on the left. Which way does the shadow of the tree point?
questions.a: To the right, away from the sun
wrong: To the left, toward the sun
questions.hint: Shadows fall on the side away from the light.
questions.fix: The tree blocks sunlight, so the shadow points away from the sun.

questions.q: Look at the plant. Which part, number 3, makes seeds?
questions.fix: The flower makes seeds after it is pollinated.

questions.q: What kind of storm is this spinning funnel?
questions.hint: It reaches down from a thunderstorm to the ground.
questions.fix: That is a tornado, a spinning column of air from a thunderstorm.

questions.q: A snowflake is made of what?
questions.fix: Snowflakes are made of ice crystals.

questions.q: What does this organ do?
questions.fix: The heart pumps blood all around your body.

questions.q: What do these two organs help you do?
questions.fix: Your lungs help you breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.

questions.q: This giant ocean animal has spots and filters tiny food from the water. Is it a whale or a shark?
questions.a: A shark, so it is a fish
wrong: A whale, so it is a mammal
questions.hint: Its name has both words in it.
questions.fix: It is a whale shark, the largest fish in the world.

questions.q: This flat animal flaps fins like wings. Is a manta ray a fish or a mammal?
questions.fix: A manta ray is a fish. It breathes underwater with gills.

questions.q: What does this insect carry from flower to flower?
questions.fix: Bees carry pollen, which helps flowers make seeds.

questions.q: How does this animal find bugs in the dark?
questions.fix: Bats make sounds and listen for echoes to find food in the dark.

questions.q: Mushrooms are not plants. What group are they in?
questions.hint: Yeast is in the same group.
questions.fix: Mushrooms are fungi, like yeast and mold.

questions.q: What covers most of the surface of this planet?
questions.fix: Oceans cover most of Earth's surface.

questions.q: What do scientists look through to see faraway planets?
questions.fix: A telescope makes faraway things look closer.
